messages.author: c91a208fffacfb7e
messages.subject: Using plotmath expressions in labels in a legend?
parts:
I see that the labs function can be used to change the title of a
legend. Is there a convenient way to incorporate expressions in the
labels in a legend? (My apologies if this is in Hadley's book - I
lent my copy to a student who has not returned it yet.)

I am trying to show comparative density curves for beta distributions
with different values of the parameters. If you look at the Wikipedia
page for the beta distribution they have density curves for alpha=0.5,
beta=0.5; alpha=5, beta=1; ...

My current code of

---- begin code ----
x <- seq(0, 1, len=201)
df <- data.frame(x = x,
d0.5_0.5 = dbeta(x, 0.5, 0.5),
d5_1 = dbeta(x, 5, 1),
d1_3 = dbeta(x, 1, 3),
d2_2 = dbeta(x, 2, 2),
d2_5 = dbeta(x, 2, 5))
fr <- melt(df, id="x", variable="Parameters")
levels(fr$Parameters) <-
c("alpha=0.5, beta=0.5", "alpha=5.0, beta=1.0",
"alpha=1.0, beta=3.0", "alpha=2.0, beta=2.0",
"alpha=2.0, beta=5.0")
print(qplot(x, value, data=fr, geom="line", color=Parameters, ylab="Density"))
---- end code ----

(It's part of an Sweave file which is why the apparently redundant
print() call isn't.)

produces the enclosed plot, which is okay but would be nicer if the
text strings "alpha" and "beta" were changed to the characters alpha
and beta. Any suggestions?

messages.author: 5a1b5a9591c118ef
messages.subject: Re: Using plotmath expressions in labels in a legend?
parts:
Hi,

I don't know if this helps but try this,

d <- data.frame(x=1:10,y=1:10,f=rep(c("alpha","beta"),each=5),
stringsAsFactors=FALSE)

value <- 3.1415
my.labs <- list(bquote(alpha==.(value)),bquote(beta==.(value)))


qplot(x,y,data=d, colour=f) +
scale_colour_manual(values=1:2, breaks=c("alpha","beta"),
labels=my.labs)


HTH,

baptiste

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: Using plotmath expressions in labels in a legend?
parts:
Hi:

It isn't perfect re alignment of decimal places, but otherwise it seems to work. Starting from your melted data frame fr,

parlabs <- list(expression(paste(alpha==0.5, ', ', ,beta==0.5)),
             expression(paste(alpha==5.0, ', ', beta==1.0)),
             expression(paste(alpha==1.0, ', ', beta==3.0)),
             expression(paste(alpha==2.0, ', ', beta==2.0)),  
             expression(paste(alpha==2.0, ', ', beta==5.0)))  
qplot(x, value, data=fr, geom="line", color=Parameters, ylab="Density") +
   scale_color_manual(breaks = levels(fr$Parameters), values = 1:5,
                      labels = parlabs) 

There is probably a more efficient way to define parlabs with bquote(), but it's something to start with.

HTH,
Dennis

messages.author: 5a1b5a9591c118ef
messages.subject: Re: Using plotmath expressions in labels in a legend?
parts:
phantom() might help with the alignment,

params <- data.frame(a=c(0.5,5,1,2,2),b=c(0.5,1,3,2,5))

labs <- mlply(params, function(a,b) {
if(length(strsplit(as.character(a),"")[[1]])==1) a <-
bquote(phantom("0.")*.(a))
if(length(strsplit(as.character(b),"")[[1]])==1) b <-
bquote(phantom("0.")*.(b))
bquote(alpha==.(a)~", "~beta==.(b)) })

HTH,

baptiste

messages.subject: Re: Using plotmath expressions in labels in a legend?
parts:
Hi:

How about this?

df <- data.frame(x = x,
           d0.5_0.5 = dbeta(x, 0.5, 0.5),
                 d5_1 = dbeta(x, 5, 1),
                 d1_3 = dbeta(x, 1, 3),
                 d2_2 = dbeta(x, 2, 2),
                 d2_5 = dbeta(x, 2, 5))
 fr <- melt(df, id="x", variable="Parameters")

params <- data.frame(a=c(0.5,5,1,2,2),b=c(0.5,1,3,2,5))
labs0 <- mlply(params, function(a,b) {
     bquote(alpha==.(sprintf('%2.1f', a))~','~beta==.(sprintf('%2.1f',b))) })

qplot(x, value, data=fr, geom="line", color=Parameters, ylab="Density") +
    scale_color_manual(breaks = levels(fr$Parameters), values = 1:5,

labels = labs0)

If we could get rid of that space before the comma, that would be ideal :)

HTH,
Dennis
